observations: Bombieri-Lagarias Theorem 2 expresses lambda_n through an alternating binomial transform of renormalized prime-power limits plus exact zeta(j)/archimedean corrections; a finite prime sum is not the theorem.

With C_j(X)=sum_{m<=X} Lambda(m)(log m)^(j-1)/m-(log X)^j/j and R_j(X)=C_j-C_j(X), the cutoff error is Delta_n(X)=-sum_{j=1}^n (-1)^(j-1) binom(n,j) R_j(X)/(j-1)!. Thus root-relevant truncation control must be aggregate and uniform over j<=n and n.

For fixed sigma<1, Guth-Maynard's exponent 30(1-sigma)/13 is positive, so its density upper bound is logically compatible with any fixed finite exceptional set and cannot alone eliminate one off-line zero.

A positive-proportion/density-one critical-line result likewise does not exclude finitely many exceptions without an integrality-tight or pointwise bridge; the short-mollifier theorem is positive-proportion, not an all-zero theorem.
Voros gives a contrastive RH-false Li-growth signature, but a proof still needs an unconditional global growth exclusion.
